_note: Check-MODE probe templates — the ground truth the linter tests its reading against. For every code example a crawl reads, the matching template runs the INSTALLED toolchain in a syntax/compile/deprecation check ONLY (never executes the code): a flagged example's surrounding prose feeds the BAD polarity prototype, a clean one's feeds GOOD. Pure DATA — adding a toolchain is an edit here, not code. `check` is argv with `{file}` substituted by a temp file holding the (prompt-stripped) snippet; a language with no entry, or whose tool is absent, is simply skipped. NEVER add an entry that runs a snippet (no `python file`, no `node file`, no shell) — check/compile flags only. `flag_markers` (optional) are stderr substrings that mark a prohibition even on a success exit (rustc's deprecation warnings) — per-tool knowledge, kept here as data.
